title: Factor a reduced algebra map through one smooth quotient-base algebra
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $\Lambda$ and $A$ commutative $R$-algebras, $A$ finitely presented over $R$ [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra], $\alpha:A\to\Lambda$ an $R$-algebra map, and $\rho\in R$. Assume $\Lambda/\rho^2\Lambda$ is a filtered colimit of smooth $R/(\rho^2)$-algebras [def-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-smooth-algebras]. There are a commutative $R/(\rho^2)$-algebra $C$ smooth over that base [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map], its induced $R$-algebra structure and scalar tower, and $R$-algebra maps $\beta:A\to C$ and $j:C\to\Lambda/\rho^2\Lambda$ such that $j(\beta(a))$ is the class of $\alpha(a)$ for every $a\in A$. If $A$ and $\Lambda$ have a common carrier universe containing that of $R$, then $C$ has that same universe. No Noetherianity or nonzerodivisor hypothesis is assumed.

source.place: Lemma Tag 07F5 (lemma-reduce-to-field), fourth paragraph: factorization through the smooth quotient-base algebra; Algebra Lemma Tag 00QO (lemma-characterize-finite-presentation), (1) implies (3), filtered form Tag 07C3

proof.text: Unpack the filtered diagram of smooth R/(ρ²)-algebras. Its colimit is also a colimit of the underlying commutative rings by [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-algebras-elementwise]. For different base and carrier universes use the explicit equivalence between CommAlgCat R/(ρ²) and rings under ULift(R/(ρ²)); the inverse restricts scalars along the inverse ring equivalence.

Regard the terms as R-algebras. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-presentation-algebra-factors-filtered-colimit] directly to the map A → Λ/(ρ²Λ), with base ULift R. The map ULift R → A is finitely presented because the original structure map is finitely presented and ULift R → R is a ring equivalence. Obtain one term C and a map β whose composite with its coprojection agrees with the reduced α and whose composite with the base structure map agrees with the structure map of C.

Evaluate the structure-map equality on ULift.up r to see that β is an R-algebra map. Restrict the coprojection to R and identify (ρ²).map(algebraMap R Λ) with the principal ideal generated by algebraMap R Λ (ρ²), using Ideal.map_span and Set.image_singleton. Composing with the resulting quotient algebra equivalence gives j and preserves the factorization equality. The selected term is smooth and has the universe specified by the original diagram. The ring structures and scalar towers are explicit restrictions, not arbitrary choices of data from an existence theorem.

lean.statement:
theorem exists_popescu_smooth_quotient_factor
    (R : Type u) (Λ : Type (max u v)) [CommRing R] [CommRing Λ] [Algebra R Λ]
    (A : Type (max u v)) [CommRing A] [Algebra R A] [Algebra.FinitePresentation R A]
    (α : A →ₐ[R] Λ) (ρ : R)
    (hmod : ObjectProperty.ind.{max u v}
      (fun B : CommAlgCat.{max u v} (R ⧸ Ideal.span {ρ ^ 2}) ↦
        Algebra.Smooth (R ⧸ Ideal.span {ρ ^ 2}) B)
      (CommAlgCat.of (R ⧸ Ideal.span {ρ ^ 2})
        (Λ ⧸ (Ideal.span {ρ ^ 2}).map (algebraMap R Λ)))) :
    ∃ (C : Type (max u v)) (_ : CommRing C) (_ : Algebra R C)
      (_ : Algebra (R ⧸ Ideal.span {ρ ^ 2}) C)
      (_ : IsScalarTower R (R ⧸ Ideal.span {ρ ^ 2}) C)
      (_ : Algebra.Smooth (R ⧸ Ideal.span {ρ ^ 2}) C)
      (β : A →ₐ[R] C)
      (j : C →ₐ[R] (Λ ⧸ Ideal.span {algebraMap R Λ (ρ ^ 2)})),
      ∀ a : A, j (β a) = Ideal.Quotient.mk _ (α a)
